answer: Unique hardware cycle anchor. Each agent identity must submit a signed measurement trace from a physically unclonable circuit, which the registry stores as its anchor and rejects any later signup reusing the same trace. A sybil farm therefore needs one distinct silicon die per identity, since cloning a trace fails challenge-response; an echo of a prior trace is refused outright. The willow rule caps enrollments per fabrication batch, so bulk-bought chips expose the operator and cost roughly the full die price plus yield loss per fake identity.
